results.content: Formally, JMMD and its concise form in a RKHS is defined as below, $$\mathbb{D}_{\mathcal{H}}(\mathcal{P}^s(\mathbf{X}^s, \mathbf{Y}^s), \mathcal{P}^t(\mathbf{X}^t, \mathbf{Y}^t)) = ||\mu_{X^s Y^s} - \mu_{X^t Y^t}||^2_{\mathcal{H}} = \text{tr}(\mathbf{K}^{XX}(\mathbf{K}^{YY} \odot \mathbf{M}^J)),$$ (1) where $\mathbf{K}^{XX}, \mathbf{K}^{YY} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ are the kernel matrices and they are computed by $k^{XX}_{ij} = k^X(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j^{\top})$, $k^{YY}_{ij} = k^Y(\mathbf{y}_i, \mathbf{y}_j^{\top})$. $k^X$ and $k^Y$ are feature and label kernels. $\mathbf{M}^J \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is the MMD matrix for JMMD.
results.route_rationale: The norm-square-to-double-sum expansion is a formalisable finite inner-product identity; it is the load-bearing algebraic content of Eq (1).

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the faithful finite core of Eq (1). For a finite sample index type with weights c (interpreted as +1/n^s on source indices and -1/n^t on target indices, so c_i c_j reproduces the M^J entries) and embedded points u_i in a real inner product space (interpreted as ψ(x)⊗φ(y)), Lean proved ‖∑ c_i u_i‖² = ∑_{ij} c_i c_j ⟨u_i,u_j⟩. With ⟨u_i,u_j⟩ = k^X_ij k^Y_ij this is exactly the expansion underlying tr(K^XX(K^YY ⊙ M^J)); the trace form assembles the same double sum via the trace-Hadamard identity (see THEOREM::1). Compiled clean, no sorry, axioms are the standard Mathlib ones.

results.route_rationale: The projected JMMD trace form reduces to a formalisable finite matrix identity once the Representer substitution Tᵀψ(x)=Bᵀk(x) is applied.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the faithful finite core of Eq (2): the matrix identity tr(Bᵀ A B) = ∑_{ij} A_ij (B Bᵀ)_ij for A : ι×ι, B : ι×κ. With A = K^XX (K^YY ⊙ M^J) K^XX, the entry (B Bᵀ)_ij is the inner product ⟨Bᵀ k_i, Bᵀ k_j⟩ of the projected features (Representer substitution), and the double sum is exactly the norm-square expansion of the left-hand side applied to the projected embeddings (the same expansion as Eq (1)). Compiled clean; the Representer substitution itself is a modelling assumption reviewed in THEOREM::2/3.

results.content: **Theorem 1** The marginal, class conditional, and weighted class conditional probability distribution distances are three special cases of JMMD with label reproducing kernels $\mathbf{K}^1$, $\mathbf{K}^2$ and $\mathbf{K}^3$, and more details about these three distances could be found in Section C of the supplementary material. $\mathbf{K}^1 = \mathbf{I}_{n \times n}$ is a matrix whose elements are all 1 with size of $n \times n$, and $\mathbf{K}^2$, $\mathbf{K}^3$ are defined as below, $$\text{k}^2_{ij} = \begin{cases} (n^s n^s)/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c} \\ (n^t n^t)/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c} \\ (n^s n^t)/(n^{s,c} n^{t,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c} \\ (n^t n^s)/(n^{t,c} n^{s,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c} \\ 0, & \text{otherwise,} \end{cases} \quad \text{k}^3_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1, & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c} \\ 1, & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c} \\ 1, & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c} \\ 1, & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c} \\ 0, & \text{otherwise,} \end{cases}$$ (3) where the superscript 's/t,c' denotes data points from the c-th class in the source/target domain.
results.route_rationale: The uniformity claim reduces to three Hadamard-product identities K¹⊙Mᴶ=Mᴹ, K²⊙Mᴶ=M^{C,c}, K³⊙Mᴶ=M^{WC,c}, which are pure piecewise matrix algebra.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised all three Hadamard identities entrywise over a finite index type with source membership isS, class label cl, fixed class c0 and positive real sizes ns nt nsc ntc. Lean proved (1) K¹⊙Mᴶ=Mᴹ (both defined identically, K¹ all-ones), (2) K²⊙Mᴶ=M^{C,c}, (3) K³⊙Mᴶ=M^{WC,c}, by case analysis on isS/cl-c0 and field_simp. These identities are the substance of Theorem 1/5; they are all correct.

results.content: $$\text{tr}(\mathbf{K}^{XX}(\mathbf{K}^{YY} \odot \mathbf{M}^H)), \quad \text{tr}(\mathbf{B}^\top \mathbf{K}^{XX}(\mathbf{K}^{YY} \odot \mathbf{M}^H)\mathbf{K}^{XX}\mathbf{B}).$$ (4) Notably, the concise HSIC is consistent with JMMD.
results.route_rationale: Definitional concise HSIC forms that mirror JMMD; there is no crisp independent assertion to machine-check beyond the algebraic form.

fallback_result.reasoning: Eq (4) presents the 'concise HSIC' in an RKHS and a projected RKHS, structurally identical to the JMMD trace forms of Eqs (1)-(2) with the JMMD matrix M^J replaced by an HSIC matrix M^H. As a definitional/modeling form it asserts no property that can be false in isolation; the substantive PSD property of the K^4 kernel used alongside it is verified in Theorem 6. No algebraic error.

results.content: $$\mathbf{k}_{ij}^4 = \begin{cases} (-n^s n^s)/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \ i \neq j \\ (n^s n^s (n^{s,c}-1))/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \ i=j \\ (-n^t n^t)/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \ i \neq j \\ (n^t n^t (n^{t,c}-1))/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \ i=j \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$ (5)
results.route_rationale: Definition of the K^4 label kernel; it asserts no property in itself (PSD is deferred to Theorem 6).

fallback_result.reasoning: Eq (5) defines the K^4 kernel: within a class, diagonal entries n^s n^s (n^{s,c}-1)/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c}) (resp. n^t n^t (n^{t,c}-1)/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c})) and off-diagonal entries -n^s n^s/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c}) (resp. -n^t n^t/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c})), zero across classes. Row sums within a class are exactly 0, consistent with a graph-Laplacian-like kernel. The definition is internally consistent; its positive-semidefiniteness is established in Theorem 6.

results.content: $$\sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^n \big(w_{ij} \|\mathbf{z}_i - \mathbf{z}_j\|_2^2\big) = \text{tr}(\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{L}\mathbf{Z}^\top),$$ (6) where $\mathbf{Z}$ is the embedding representation of $\mathbf{X}$. $\mathbf{L} = \mathbf{Q} - \mathbf{W}$ is the graph Laplacian matrix where $\mathbf{Q} = \text{diag}(\mathbf{q}_1, \cdots, \mathbf{q}_n)$ is a diagonal matrix and $\mathbf{q}_i = \sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}$.
results.route_rationale: Graph-Laplacian quadratic-form identity; formalisable, and the factor of 2 in the double-sum version is machine-checkable.

lean_result.reasoning: The printed identity ∑_{i,j} w_ij‖z_i-z_j‖² = tr(Z L Zᵀ) is FALSE as written: the double sum over ordered pairs carries a factor 2. Lean proved the corrected identity graph_laplacian_scalar: ∑_{i,j} w_ij (x_i-x_j)² = 2·(∑_i q_i x_i² − ∑_{i,j} w_ij x_i x_j) = 2·xᵀ L x for symmetric w (q_i = ∑_j w_ij). Lean also proved a concrete counterexample paper_eq6_factor_free_false: for w≡1 and x=[0,1] on Fin 2, the left side is 2 while xᵀ L x is 1, so the paper's equality fails. The factor 2 does not change the minimizer of the objective or the sign-based qualitative claims, so the error is minor, but the printed equality is mathematically false.

lean.formal_statement: theorem graph_laplacian_scalar : (∑ i, ∑ j, w i j * (x i - x j)^2) = 2 * ((∑ i, (∑ j, w i j) * (x i)^2) - (∑ i, ∑ j, w i j * x i * x j))  [corrected, PASSED]; theorem paper_eq6_factor_free_false : ¬ (∑ i : Fin 2, ∑ j : Fin 2, 1 * (x0 i - x0 j)^2 = x0 0 * (2*x0 0 - (x0 0 + x0 1)) + x0 1 * (2*x0 1 - (x0 0 + x0 1)))  [refutes the printed equality]

results.content: $$w_{ij}^J = \begin{cases} -1/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \ \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c} \\ -1/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \ \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c} \\ 1/(n^{s,c} n^{t,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \ \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c} \\ 1/(n^{t,c} n^{s,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \ \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c} \\ 0, & \text{otherwise,} \end{cases} \quad w_{ij}^H = \begin{cases} 1/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c}, \ \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{s,c} \\ 1/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c}), & \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c}, \ \mathbf{x}_j \in \mathcal{D}^{t,c} \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$ (7)
results.route_rationale: Weight-matrix definitions plus the qualitative sign interpretation; no crisp formal assertion beyond the sign pattern.

fallback_result.reasoning: Eq (7) defines the similarity weights W^J and W^H. Since the objective is ∑_{ij} w_ij‖z_i−z_j‖² to be minimised, a negative weight pushes the pair apart and a positive weight draws it together. W^J is negative for same-class-same-domain pairs (pushing them apart) and positive for same-class cross-domain pairs (drawing them together); W^H is positive for same-class-same-domain pairs (intra-class compactness). The textual interpretation that JMMD's same-domain weights are opposite in sign to HSIC's is correct.

results.content: $$\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\big(w_{ij}^{J}\|\mathbf{B}^{\top}\mathbf{k}_{i}^{XX}-\mathbf{B}^{\top}\mathbf{k}_{j}^{XX}\|_{F}^{2}\big),\quad \sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\big(w_{ij}^{H}\|\mathbf{B}^{\top}\mathbf{k}_{i}^{XX}-\mathbf{B}^{\top}\mathbf{k}_{j}^{XX}\|_{F}^{2}\big),\quad (8)$$ where $\mathbf{B}^{\top}\mathbf{k}^{XX}$ is the embedded feature representation and (8) is similar to (6).
results.route_rationale: The rewritten JMMD/HSIC forms equal the projected losses up to the same constant factor as Eq (6); informal review is appropriate given the constant-factor convention.

fallback_result.reasoning: Eq (8) rewrites the projected JMMD/HSIC as the weighted double sums ∑ w^J_ij ‖Bᵀk_i−Bᵀk_j‖²_F and ∑ w^H_ij ‖Bᵀk_i−Bᵀk_j‖²_F. With the degree matrices Q^J and Q^H both zero (each row of W^J and W^H sums to zero), the graph-Laplacian identity gives ∑ w^J_ij ‖·‖² = 2·tr(BᵀK^XX M^{C,c} K^XX B), i.e. the equality with the projected JMMD holds only up to the same factor 2 already identified in Eq (6) (see the paper::EQUATION::4 finding). The constant factor does not change the minimizer or the sign interpretation, so this is not a new independent error; the qualitative/graph-embedding reading is sound.

results.content: $$\operatorname{tr}\big(\mathbf{K}^{XX}(\mathbf{K}^{J}\odot\mathbf{M}^{J}+\delta\,\mathbf{K}^{H}\odot\mathbf{M}^{H})\big),\quad \operatorname{tr}\big(\mathbf{B}^{\top}\mathbf{K}^{XX}(\mathbf{K}^{J}\odot\mathbf{M}^{J}+\delta\,\mathbf{K}^{H}\odot\mathbf{M}^{H})\mathbf{K}^{XX}\mathbf{B}\big),\quad (9)$$ where $\delta$ aims to balance the relative importance between JMMD and HSIC, and we can adopt $\mathbf{K}^{1}$, $\mathbf{K}^{2}$ or $\mathbf{K}^{3}$ for $\mathbf{K}^{J}$ and $\mathbf{K}^{4}$ for $\mathbf{K}^{H}$. ... its partial derivative with respect to $\mathbf{B}$ is $2\mathbf{K}^{XX}(\mathbf{K}^{J}\odot\mathbf{M}^{J}+\delta\,\mathbf{K}^{H}\odot\mathbf{M}^{H})\mathbf{K}^{XX}\mathbf{B}$.
results.route_rationale: The partial-derivative claim d/dB tr(BᵀAB)=2AB for symmetric A is formalisable matrix calculus.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the derivative claim. For L*(B)=tr(Bᵀ A B) with A = K^XX(K^J⊙M^J+δK^H⊙M^H)K^XX symmetric, Lean proved the bilinear expansion tr((B+H)ᵀ A (B+H)) = tr(BᵀAB) + [tr(BᵀAH)+tr(HᵀAB)] + tr(HᵀAH), and that the linear part tr(BᵀAH)+tr(HᵀAB) equals tr(Hᵀ(2·A·B)) for symmetric A. Hence the gradient of tr(BᵀAB) w.r.t. B is 2AB — exactly the paper's formula 2K^XX(K^J⊙M^J+δK^H⊙M^H)K^XXB.

results.content: $$\mathbb{D}_{\mathcal{H}}\left(P^s(\mathbf{X}^s),P^t(\mathbf{X}^t)\right) =\left\|\mathbb{E}\big(\psi(\mathbf{X}^s)\big)-\mathbb{E}\big(\psi(\mathbf{X}^t)\big)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 =\left\|\mu_{X^s}-\mu_{X^t}\right\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 =\left\|\frac{1}{n^s}\sum_{i=1}^{n^s}\psi(\mathbf{x}_i)-\frac{1}{n^t}\sum_{j=1}^{n^t}\psi(\mathbf{x}_j)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 =\operatorname{tr}\left(\mathbf{K}^{XX}\mathbf{M}^M\right),$$ (30) where $\mathbf{K}^{XX}=\psi(\mathbf{X})^\top\psi(\mathbf{X})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $k^{XX}_{ij}=k^X(\mathbf{x}_i,\mathbf{x}_j)$. The MMD matrix: $m_{ij}^M = 1/(n^s n^s)$ if $\mathbf{x}_i,\mathbf{x}_j\in\mathcal{D}^s$; $1/(n^t n^t)$ if $\mathbf{x}_i,\mathbf{x}_j\in\mathcal{D}^t$; $-1/(n^s n^t)$ otherwise. (31)
results.route_rationale: Standard textbook MMD trace identity; known result verified by inspection.

fallback_result.reasoning: Eq (30) is the standard MMD identity: expanding ‖(1/n^s)∑_s ψ(x_i) − (1/n^t)∑_t ψ(x_j)‖² gives (1/n^s n^s)∑_{i,i'∈s}k_{ii'} + (1/n^t n^t)∑_{j,j'∈t}k_{jj'} − (2/n^s n^t)∑_{i∈s,j∈t}k_{ij}, which equals tr(K^XX M^M) with the printed M^M (1/(n^s n^s) both-source, 1/(n^t n^t) both-target, −1/(n^s n^t) cross; the cross terms appear twice and give the −2 factor). Correct.

results.content: $$\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{H}}\left(\mathcal{P}^s(\mathbf{X}^s|\mathbf{Y}^s), \mathcal{P}^t(\mathbf{X}^t|\mathbf{Y}^t)\right) = \sum_{c=1}^{C} \left\| \frac{1}{n^{s,c}} \sum_{i=1}^{n^{s,c}} \psi(\mathbf{x}_i) - \frac{1}{n^{t,c}} \sum_{j=1}^{n^{t,c}} \psi(\mathbf{x}_j) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 = \sum_{c=1}^{C} \mathrm{tr}\left(\mathbf{K}^{\mathbf{XX}} \mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{C},c}\right),$$ (32) with $m_{ij}^{\mathrm{C},c} = 1/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c})$ both source class c; $1/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c})$ both target class c; $-1/(n^{s,c} n^{t,c})$ source c to target c; $-1/(n^{t,c} n^{s,c})$ target c to source c; $0$ otherwise. (33)
results.route_rationale: Standard class-wise MMD (CMMD) formula; known result verified by inspection.

fallback_result.reasoning: Eq (32) is the standard class-wise MMD: the trace identity holds per class with the class-normalised coefficients, exactly as for MMD applied within class c. The M^{C,c} entries (1/(n^{s,c}n^{s,c}), 1/(n^{t,c}n^{t,c}), −1/(n^{s,c}n^{t,c}) cross) reproduce the per-class expansion. Correct.

results.location: C.3 Weighted Class-Wise Maximum Mean Discrepancy
results.content: $$\sum_{c=1}^{C} \left\| \frac{\mathcal{P}^s(y^s=c)}{n^{s,c}} \sum_{i=1}^{n^{s,c}} \psi(\mathbf{x}_i) - \frac{\mathcal{P}^t(y^t=c)}{n^{t,c}} \sum_{j=1}^{n^{t,c}} \psi(\mathbf{x}_j) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 = \sum_{c=1}^{C} \left\| \frac{1}{n^s} \sum_{i=1}^{n^{s,c}} \psi(\mathbf{x}_i) - \frac{1}{n^t} \sum_{j=1}^{n^{t,c}} \psi(\mathbf{x}_j) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 = \sum_{c=1}^{C} \mathrm{tr}\left(\mathbf{K}^{\mathbf{XX}} \mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{WC},c}\right),$$ (34) with $m_{ij}^{\mathrm{WC},c} = 1/(n^s n^s)$ both source class c; $1/(n^t n^t)$ both target class c; $-1/(n^s n^t)$ cross; $0$ otherwise. (35)
results.route_rationale: Standard weighted class-wise MMD; check the class-prior step P^s(y=c)/n^{s,c} = 1/n^s.

fallback_result.reasoning: Eq (34) is the standard weighted class-wise MMD. The first equality uses the empirical class prior P^s(y^s=c) = n^{s,c}/n^s (and likewise for t), so P^s(y^s=c)/n^{s,c} = 1/n^s and P^t(y^t=c)/n^{t,c} = 1/n^t — valid for empirical priors. The trace identity then holds with M^{WC,c} using domain sizes n^s, n^t inside each class block, zero outside. Correct.

results.location: A Concise JMMD in an RKHS
results.content: Theorem 2. In an RKHS, JMMD could be rewritten as the following concise form, $$\mathbb{D}_{\mathcal{H}}\left(\mathcal{P}^s(\mathbf{X}^s, \mathbf{Y}^s), \mathcal{P}^t(\mathbf{X}^t, \mathbf{Y}^t)\right) = \left\|\frac{1}{n^s}\sum_{i=1}^{n^s}\left(\psi(\mathbf{x}_i^s)\otimes\phi(\mathbf{y}_i^s)\right) - \frac{1}{n^t}\sum_{j=1}^{n^t}\left(\psi(\mathbf{x}_j^t)\otimes\phi(\mathbf{y}_j^t)\right)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 = \mathrm{tr}\!\left(\mathbf{K}^{XX}\!\left(\mathbf{K}^{YY}\odot\mathbf{M}^J\right)\right),$$ (10) Proof: ... (block-matrix expansion, Eqs (11)-(18); the proof cites $\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{A}\odot \mathbf{B}\mathbf{C})=\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{B}\odot \mathbf{C}))$ for symmetric A,B,C to pass from the block form to the concise form.)
results.route_rationale: The trace-Hadamard associativity identity used in the proof is a formalisable matrix identity (and the printed statement is ambiguous enough to warrant a machine check).

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the identity the proof actually needs: tr((A⊙B)C) = tr(A(B⊙C)) for symmetric B, which is exactly the step from the block form tr((K^XX⊙K^YY)M^J) to the concise form tr(K^XX(K^YY⊙M^J)) with A=K^XX, B=K^YY, C=M^J. Lean proved it (paper__THEOREM__1). Note on the printed string 'tr(A⊙BC)': read left-to-right as tr((A⊙B)C) it is the standard, correct identity; read as tr(A⊙(BC)) it would be false in general, but that reading is not the one the derivation requires, so this is notation ambiguity rather than a mathematical error in the result.

results.location: B A Concise JMMD in a Projected RKHS
results.content: Theorem 3 In a projected RKHS, JMMD could be rewritten as the following concise form, $$\mathbb{D}_{\mathcal{H}}\left(P^s(\mathbf{X}^s,\mathbf{Y}^s),\,P^t(\mathbf{X}^t,\mathbf{Y}^t)\right) = \left\|\frac{1}{n^s}\sum_{i=1}^{n^s}\big(\mathbf{T}^\top\psi(\mathbf{x}_i^s)\otimes \phi(\mathbf{y}_i^s)\big) - \frac{1}{n^t}\sum_{j=1}^{n^t}\big(\mathbf{T}^\top\psi(\mathbf{x}_j^t)\otimes \phi(\mathbf{y}_j^t)\big)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 = \operatorname{tr}\!\left(\mathbf{B}^\top \mathbf{K}^{XX}(\mathbf{K}^{YY}\odot \mathbf{M}^J)\mathbf{K}^{XX}\mathbf{B}\right).$$ (19) Proof: Representer substitution $\mathbf{T}^\top\psi(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf{b}_i k^X(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}_i)$ (Eq 20), then the Θ^s, Θ^t block expansion (Eqs (21)-(29)).
results.route_rationale: The derivation rests on the infinite-dimensional Representer substitution plus the same finite expansion/trace identities already machine-checked in EQUATION::0, EQUATION::1 and THEOREM::1; the RKHS framing is not faithfully formalisable in budget.

fallback_result.reasoning: Theorem 3 applies the Representer substitution Tᵀψ(x)=∑ᵢ bᵢ k^X(x,xᵢ) (so the projected feature is Bᵀk(x)), then repeats the Theorem-2 block expansion. The projected-feature inner product ⟨Bᵀk_i, Bᵀk_j⟩ = k_iᵀBBᵀk_j = (K^XX BBᵀ K^XX)_ij, and assembling the Θ blocks gives tr(BᵀK^XX(K^YY⊙M^J)K^XXB). Each finite-algebra step is machine-checked (EQUATION::0 expansion, EQUATION::1 trace identity, THEOREM::1 trace-Hadamard). Given the Representer substitution (a standing modelling assumption, Theorem 4), the derivation is correct.

results.location: B A Concise JMMD in a Projected RKHS
results.content: Theorem 4 (Representer theorem) It says that any function can be decomposed into finite values of a kernel function with corresponding coefficients [23]. $$\mathbf{T}^\top\psi(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(\mathbf{b}_i\,k^X(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}_i)\big) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(\mathbf{b}_i\langle\psi(\mathbf{x}),\psi(\mathbf{x}_i)\rangle\big) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(\mathbf{b}_i\,\psi(\mathbf{x}_i)^\top\psi(\mathbf{x})\big),$$ (20)
results.route_rationale: Classical functional-analysis theorem restated; the general theorem is not faithfully formalisable within budget and the specific substitution is a standing modelling assumption.

fallback_result.reasoning: Theorem 4 restates the classical Representer theorem. The loose prose ('any function can be decomposed into finite values of a kernel function') is a compressed paraphrase — the actual theorem says the regularized-risk minimizer in an RKHS lies in the span of the training-point kernel evaluations — but the specific application Tᵀψ(x)=∑ᵢ bᵢ k^X(x,xᵢ) is the standard representer substitution used throughout the subspace-learning literature, and it is a legitimate modelling assumption here. No derivation error in the paper's own use.

results.content: Theorem 5 The marginal, class-conditional and weighted class-conditional probability distribution distances are three special cases of JMMD with label reproducing kernels $\mathbf{K}^1$, $\mathbf{K}^2$ and $\mathbf{K}^3$. ... Proof: ... It is easy to verify that $\mathbf{K}^1\odot\mathbf{M}^J=\mathbf{M}^M$, $\mathbf{K}^2\odot\mathbf{M}^J=\mathbf{M}^{C,c}$ and $\mathbf{K}^3\odot\mathbf{M}^J=\mathbf{M}^{WC,c}$. Therefore, the marginal, class conditional and weighted class conditional probability distribution distances are three special cases of JMMD with different label reproducing kernels.
results.route_rationale: Same claims as Theorem 1, whose identities were machine-checked (paper::THEOREM::0 PASSED); informal proof review here.

fallback_result.reasoning: Theorem 5 repeats the uniformity claim of Theorem 1 and proves it by the three Hadamard identities K¹⊙M^J=M^M, K²⊙M^J=M^{C,c}, K³⊙M^J=M^{WC,c}. These identities were formally verified in Lean (paper::THEOREM::0, PASSED). The proof is correct.

results.content: Theorem 6 $\mathbf{K}^1$, $\mathbf{K}^2$, $\mathbf{K}^3$ and $\mathbf{K}^4$ are the reproducing kernels. Proof: For K^1,K^2,K^3, the Gram matrices decompose as $\mathbf{G}^1=\mathbf{p}^1\mathbf{p}^{1\top}$, $\mathbf{G}^{2,c}=\mathbf{p}^{2,c}\mathbf{p}^{2,c\top}$, $\mathbf{G}^{3,c}=\mathbf{p}^{3,c}\mathbf{p}^{3,c\top}$ (rank-one, hence PSD). For K^4: $\mathbf{x}^\top\mathbf{G}^4\mathbf{x} = \sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2 \ge 0$ (45) with $w_{ij} = (n^s n^s)/(n^{s,c} n^{s,c})$ both source class c, $(n^t n^t)/(n^{t,c} n^{t,c})$ both target class c, $0$ otherwise. (46)
results.route_rationale: PSD proofs via rank-one decompositions and the graph-Laplacian quadratic form; the graph-Laplacian identity is machine-checked in EQUATION::4.

fallback_result.reasoning: K^1 = 1_n 1_nᵀ, and G^{2,c}=p^{2,c}(p^{2,c})ᵀ, G^{3,c}=p^{3,c}(p^{3,c})ᵀ are rank-one positive-semidefinite, so K^2=Σ_c G^{2,c} and K^3=Σ_c G^{3,c} are PSD — correct. For K^4, the Gram matrix equals Q−W (checked: diagonal n^s n^s(n^{s,c}−1)/(n^{s,c}n^{s,c}), off-diagonal −n^s n^s/(n^{s,c}n^{s,c}), row sums 0), so xᵀG^4x = (1/2)∑_{ij} w_ij(x_i−x_j)² ≥ 0 by the graph-Laplacian identity. The printed Eq (45) omits the 1/2 (same factor-2 convention as Eq (6), see paper::EQUATION::4 finding), but since w_ij ≥ 0 the ≥ 0 conclusion is unaffected and the PSD claim is correct.

findings.evidence: Lean refuted the factor-free graph-Laplacian identity as printed. For two points with weights $w_{ij}=1$ and $\mathbf{z}=[0,1]^{\top}$, $\sum_{i,j}w_{ij}\|\mathbf{z}_i-\mathbf{z}_j\|^2 = 2$ while $\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{L}\mathbf{Z}^{\top}) = \mathbf{z}^{\top}\mathbf{L}\mathbf{z} = 1$ (concrete counterexample proved in Lean). The correct identity is $\sum_{i,j}w_{ij}\|\mathbf{z}_i-\mathbf{z}_j\|^2 = 2\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{L}\mathbf{Z}^{\top})$, which Lean also proved. The missing factor 2 is a constant scale in the objective: it does not change the minimizer or the sign-based qualitative claims (JMMD pushing same-class-same-domain apart, HSIC drawing them together), but the printed equality is mathematically false as written. The same factor-2 convention appears in Eq (8) and Eq (45) without affecting those conclusions.

summary: Verified the mathematics of the JMMD/HSIC paper. 17 snippets were extracted: 11 equations, 6 theorems. Six were routed to Lean 4 (one shared project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper) and eleven to informal review; no Lean FAILED results, so no fallbacks were needed. Lean settled the core finite-algebra content: the JMMD norm-square/trace identity (Eq 1), the projected-JMMD trace identity (Eq 2), the three uniformity Hadamard identities K^1⊙M^J=M^M, K^2⊙M^J=M^{C,c}, K^3⊙M^J=M^{WC,c} (Theorem 1/5), the derivative of tr(B^TAB) being 2AB (Eq 9), and the trace-Hadamard associativity tr((A⊙B)C)=tr(A(B⊙C)) used in the proof of Theorem 2 — all PASSED. One formal refutation was obtained: the graph-Laplacian identity (Eq 6) as printed omits a factor 2 (double sum over ordered pairs gives 2·tr(ZLZ^T), not tr(ZLZ^T)); Lean proved a concrete counterexample plus the corrected identity. This is a minor, constant-scale error that does not invalidate the paper's main theoretical claims (the uniformity of JMMD and the sign-based graph-embedding interpretation are unaffected). The same factor-2 convention also appears in Eq (8) and Eq (45) without changing those conclusions. Informal review found the MMD/CMMD/WCMMD formulas, the K^4 PSD proof, and the Representer-based projected-JMMD derivation to be correct. The Lean project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper was reused (it pre-existed with another paper's verified artifacts and was not created by this run), so it was left on disk and lean_project_kept is true. Verdict: MINOR_ERRORS — one confident minor finding, no critical errors.
